articles.title: Deion Sanders steps in to help Jimmy Horn Jr., his son Shedeur's “brother,” after he was cut by the Panthers
articles.standfirst: Coach Prime immediately backed his former Colorado receiver
articles.summary: Coach Prime immediately backed his former Colorado receiver
articles.body:
Deion Sanders did more than offer sympathy when Jimmy Horn Jr. suddenly found himself without an NFL team.

The Colorado coach said he immediately began making calls after the Carolina Panthers waived Horn , the former Buffaloes receiver whom Shedeur Sanders has described as a brother.

Horn’s release came shortly after a costly special-teams mistake in Carolina’s 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears .

“I made some calls too… immediately,” Sanders said when asked about the move Wednesday.

Horn had muffed a second-quarter punt against Chicago, helping set up a Bears field goal at a point when the game was still competitive. Sanders acknowledged the error but pushed back strongly against any suggestion that Horn’s character had anything to do with the Panthers’ decision.

“I don’t understand how it’s… and I hate questioning management because I’m not there, but this kid is a great human being,” Sanders said.

One story that sums up Horn

Sanders has known Horn since coaching him at Colorado in 2023 and 2024, and he used a small off-field example to explain why he continues to defend him so strongly.

“The best thing I heard, the story about this kid, you know we get our kids car deals and all of that, right?” Sanders said.

“The dealer that I know that a lot of our kids get car deals for, it’s only one guy who ever turned their car back in cleaned and a tank full of gas and that was Jimmy Horn. Says a lot about who he is.”

Sanders was also careful not to excuse what happened against Chicago.

“Okay, he dropped the punt. I get it. I understand,” he said. “But if you was just wanting to get rid of him, it wasn’t about character, I promise you that.”

Horn entered the NFL as a sixth-round pick in 2025, selected No.208 overall by Carolina. He finished his rookie season with 11 catches for 108 yards after producing 1,001 receiving yards and seven touchdowns across two seasons at Colorado.

Bond with the Sanders family runs deep

The connection between Horn and the Sanders family has long extended beyond the field. Deion Sanders had promised Horn’s father, who was incarcerated at the time, that he would look after his son.

The coach later walked with Horn on Senior Day and has spoken of him with unusual affection. Shedeur Sanders has been just as open about their relationship.

“Jimmy definitely is missed,” Shedeur said last year while reflecting on former Colorado teammates. “A lot of the Colorado players are missed. All of them have different personalities. And Jimmy, I miss seeing his smile when we’re at practice with his gold grillz.”

Horn has also remained in touch with Deion during difficult moments, including after Sanders revealed his bladder cancer diagnosis. Horn has now cleared waivers and is a free agent, meaning another team can sign him without submitting a claim.

His next opportunity is uncertain. What isn't uncertain is that Sanders is already working to help create one.

articles.title: The Panthers' major decision regarding their coaching staff following the tough loss to the Packers
articles.standfirst: Panthers turn to experienced NFL coach Todd Wash following defensive struggles
articles.summary: Panthers turn to experienced NFL coach Todd Wash following defensive struggles
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers have made significant changes to their coaching staff following Thursday night's disappointing 27-19 defeat against the Green Bay Packers.

Head coach Dave Canales has decided to take a different approach defensively, dismissing defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley on Friday.

The decision comes as Carolina attempts to turn its season around after falling to a 3-4 record. The team's defensive performances have become a major concern, particularly against the run, where the Panthers have struggled to prevent opponents from gaining significant yardage.

Carolina entered the week ranked 22nd in total defense and last in the NFL against the run. Their latest defeat against Green Bay only increased the pressure on the coaching staff.

Packers quarterback Jordan Love completed 30 of 41 passing attempts for 288 yards, three touchdowns and one interception.

Injuries have also played a role in Carolina's defensive struggles. Starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson have missed recent games, while backup cornerback Akayleb Evans was placed on injured reserve earlier this week.

Their absences have left the Panthers with fewer options in the secondary.

Dave Canales explains his decision as Todd Wash takes charge

Speaking about the coaching changes, Canales explained that the decision followed an extensive evaluation of the team's performances and its remaining opportunities this season.

"There's just collecting a lot of information over the course of our time that really led to the decision," Canales stated.

"Ultimately—when I look at how many games we have in front of us, the position we're at in the division and really just wanted to get the most out of our guys.

"And really, making that decision, I take that responsibility very seriously as the head coach, and I know it's my responsibility to put the players in a position where they feel confident, where they feel ready to go.

The coaching changes see defensive line coach Todd Wash promoted to interim defensive coordinator. He'll also take responsibility for calling defensive plays, giving him an immediate opportunity to reshape the unit.

Wash brings considerable experience to the position, having spent 31 years coaching football, including 20 seasons in the NFL. He joined Carolina in 2023 and previously served as defensive coordinator of the Jacksonville Jaguars for five seasons.

His most notable achievement came in 2017, when Jacksonville finished with the league's second-ranked defense before reaching the AFC Championship Game.

Meanwhile, outside linebackers coach and run game specialist AC Carter will receive additional responsibilities overseeing the defensive line. Secondary coach Renaldo Hill will continue managing the defensive backs.

Canales also confirmed that owner David Tepper and general manager Dan Morgan were consulted before the decision was made.

The dismissals represent a significant turning point for the Panthers as they attempt to get their 2026 campaign back on track.
